facts.evidence: "Reported net revenue was $57.3 billion; managed net revenue (non-GAAP) was $58.0 billion, up 27% year-over-year." — the $58.0B/27% pairing is correctly labeled managed (non-GAAP), and the $57.3B reported figure is correct (the 28% reported growth rate is not given, but no figure is mismatched).
"Reported net income was $21.2 billion ($7.70 per share)"
"net income excluding significant items (non-GAAP) was $16.9 billion ($6.14 per share)"

"with Markets revenue up 35%"; "Markets revenue increased 35% year-over-year, with Equity Markets up 86%, driven by elevated client activity." — growth rate and Equity Markets driver are correct; the $12.1 billion dollar amount is not given, but nothing stated is wrong.
"return on tangible common equity (ROTCE, non-GAAP) was 29%, or 23% excluding significant items"

"Corporate net income was $4.2 billion, up $2.5 billion year-over-year, primarily due to a $4.6 billion net gain related to Visa shares."; "the $4.6 billion Visa gain and $1.0 billion equity investment gains"
"The firm distributed $4.0 billion in common dividends and $6.2 billion in common stock net repurchases during the quarter."
"Basel III common equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio was 14.1% (Standardized) and 14.2% (Advanced)." — release flags both as estimated; the brief omits that qualifier but the figures are right.

"Review credit costs, which were $2.5 billion, including a $149 million net reserve build primarily in Wholesale" — the $2.5B provision and reserve build are correct; the $2.4 billion of net charge-offs is not mentioned.

claims.claim: Revenue in each of JPMorgan's lines of business hit a new record in Q2 2026.
Reported net income was $21.2 billion, or $7.70 per share.
Net income excluding significant items (non-GAAP) was $16.9 billion, or $6.14 per share.
Reported net revenue was $57.3 billion.
Managed net revenue (non-GAAP) was $58.0 billion, up 27% year-over-year.
Noninterest expense was $27.3 billion.
The reported overhead ratio was 48% and the managed overhead ratio (non-GAAP) was 47%.
Return on common equity (ROE) was 24%.
Return on tangible common equity (ROTCE, non-GAAP) was 29%, or 23% excluding significant items.
CIB net income was $9.7 billion, up 46% year-over-year.
CIB Markets revenue was up 35% year-over-year.
Investment Banking fees were up 30% year-over-year.
CCB net income was $5.3 billion, up 3% year-over-year.
CCB's net income growth was driven by Card Services & Auto revenue growth of 12%.
claims.note: The 12% Card Services & Auto revenue growth is correct, but the release attributes it to CCB net revenue growth (+8%), not to the 3% net income growth; CCB noninterest expense rose 13% and no such causal link for net income is stated.

claims.claim: AWM net income was $2.0 billion, up 33% year-over-year.
AWM assets under management were $5.1 trillion, up 18% year-over-year.
Corporate net income was $4.2 billion, up $2.5 billion year-over-year.
The Corporate increase was primarily due to a $4.6 billion net gain related to Visa shares.
The release does not provide specific quantitative guidance or outlook figures for future periods.
Management noted that market sentiment remains constructive for continued activity, particularly in Investment Banking.
CEO Jamie Dimon cited risks including geopolitical tensions, sticky inflation and elevated asset prices, and said the Firm prepares for a wide range of scenarios.
The Basel III CET1 capital ratio was 14.1% Standardized and 14.2% Advanced.
The firm distributed $4.0 billion in common dividends and $6.2 billion of common stock net repurchases during the quarter.
Book value per share was $133.01, up 9% year-over-year.
Tangible book value per share (non-GAAP) was $113.35, up 10% year-over-year.
Equity Markets revenue was up 86% year-over-year.
Markets revenue growth was driven by elevated client activity.
The $4.6 billion Visa gain and $1.0 billion of equity investment gains account for the difference between reported and non-GAAP (ex-significant-items) net income.
Credit costs were $2.5 billion, including a $149 million net reserve build primarily in Wholesale.
Average loans were up 10% year-over-year.
